item.title: Health and Safety Concern – Unremoved Tree Cuttings, 27th July
item.description:
I would like to report what I believe is a health and safety concern. A tree or large shrub near Stephen’s house has recently been cut back, which I understand was necessary as it had become overgrown and was obstructing the pathway. However, all of the cut branches and woody shrubs have been left on the ground behind the fence and has not been cleared away. Given the current hot, dry weather, I am concerned that this poses a potential fire risk. It would only take something like a discarded cigarette for the dry vegetation to catch alight. Aside from the safety concern, it also leaves the area looking untidy. Could this please be inspected and the cuttings removed as soon as possible? Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 134, Thurlow Park Road, Dulwich, Greater London

item.title: Overgrown grass and weeds - forgotten, 27th July
item.description:
Dear Bromley Council, I am writing to raise a formal complaint about the continued lack of grass cutting and maintenance in our local area. The grass has once again been left to become severely overgrown, and this is now causing environmental and public health concerns. Long grass provides a habitat for pests such as ticks and rodents, which can pose a risk to children and pets using the area. It also makes it difficult for families to enjoy the green space safely. In addition, the area has become increasingly littered. The combination of overgrown vegetation and accumulated rubbish creates an unpleasant environment, encourages further fly-tipping and littering, and detracts from the appearance of the neighbourhood. This is now another year in which the grass has not been cut to an acceptable standard. Residents should not have to repeatedly raise the same issue. Regular maintenance is essential to keep our community clean, safe, and accessible for everyone. I would appreciate it if the Council could investigate this matter as a priority and provide an update on when the grass will be cut, the litter removed, and what measures will be taken to prevent this situation from recurring. I look forward to your response. Yours faithfully Anna

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Station Approach, Poverest, Greater London
